svg.title: Arthritis sorted by its synovial fluid: non-inflammatory fluid (clear, viscous, under 2000 white cells) is osteoarthritis or trauma; infectious fluid (cloudy, low viscosity, over 75% neutrophils, positive Gram stain and culture) is septic arthritis; inflammatory fluid (cloudy, over 2000 cells, over 50% neutrophils) is then split by crystals (gout, pseudogout), RF and anti-CCP (rheumatoid arthritis), HLA-B27 with negative serology (ankylosing spondylitis, psoriatic and reactive arthritis), or a positive ANA (connective tissue disease)

svg.text: then blood tests for what the fluid and history point to: ESR, CRP · RF, anti-CCP · ANA → ENA, dsDNA, C3, C4
